rules.law_name: San Francisco Rent Ordinance Just Cause Eviction Protections
rules.title: Just cause required for evictions from covered rental units
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance only for one of the listed just-cause reasons, and that reason must be the dominant motive for the eviction. Expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership is not just cause.

coverage.other_unresolvable: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance; the document notes that some tenancies exempt from rent increase limitations are still subject to the eviction provisions.
coverage.summary: Covers tenants in rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance, including some tenancies not covered by the Ordinance’s rent-increase limits.

rules.penalty: If a landlord evicts or tries to evict a tenant unlawfully, the landlord may be subject to substantial civil and/or criminal liability.
rules.interaction: The document states that some tenancies exempt from the Ordinance’s rent increase limitations, including newly constructed units with a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 and Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies, are still subject to the Ordinance’s eviction provisions.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction.
